Planning and prompting

# Maximize token efficiency

Spend fewer tokens in Bolt without slowing down. Learn what burns tokens fastest, how to prompt efficiently, when to clear context, and which agent to pick.

Tokens are small pieces of text that AI uses to read and generate content. Short, common words are typically one token each, but longer or less common words can be several. Bolt consumes tokens when it reads your prompts and project files, thinks, responds to your prompts, and builds in your project.

Managing token use is related to managing context. Bolt processes fewer tokens when it has less context to process, so keeping your context low improves both performance and token efficiency. To get the most out of your tokens, combine these strategies with ways to [manage project context](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/manage-context).

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#plan-before-you-build)

Plan before you build

Planning your app before you start building can save time and tokens by helping you avoid rework later. Decide what type of app you’re making, who it’s for, and the key features you need, then write a clear first prompt and build step by step. To learn more about project planning, see [Project lifecycle](https://support.bolt.new/get-started/project-lifecycle). Use [Plan mode](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/plan-mode) to talk through your plan, troubleshoot, or make decisions with Bolt without changing your code. In Build mode, every prompt you submit updates your code and uses tokens, but Plan mode uses fewer tokens because it doesn’t make any changes to your project.

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#choose-the-right-agent-for-efficient-token-use)

Choose the right agent for efficient token use

Each Bolt agent uses tokens differently. For tasks of average complexity, the Standard agent gives you accurate results without the additional token cost of deeper reasoning. For more complex tasks, the Max agent uses more tokens to work through the full scope of your task. Using the Max agent for straightforward tasks may use more tokens than necessary, and using the Standard agent for complex tasks may require more prompts to achieve your goal. To use tokens effectively, [choose the agent](https://support.bolt.new/building/agents) best suited to your task.

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#keep-your-prompts-specific-and-focused)

Keep your prompts specific and focused

When prompting, be clear and specific. Tell the agent to focus on specific files or functions rather than the entire codebase. See [Prompt effectively](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/prompting-effectively) for more detailed guidance on prompting.

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#use-buttons-instead-of-prompting-where-possible)

Use buttons instead of prompting where possible

Whenever they’re available, use buttons and built-in actions rather than asking Bolt to do the same task for you. For example:

*   Use the Publish button instead of prompting Bolt to [publish your site](https://support.bolt.new/bolt-cloud/hosting/publish).
*   Use the Version History feature instead of prompting Bolt to [revert to a previous version of your project](https://support.bolt.new/managing-projects/rollback-backup#restore-using-version-history).

Clicking an on-screen button or action doesn’t use tokens, but prompting Bolt does.

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#add-functionality-incrementally)

Add functionality incrementally

Before adding advanced functionality, make sure your project’s basic functionality is in place.

*   **Create your core pages:** For example, a homepage, a dashboard, and a basic contact or help page
*   **Set up navigation:** Make sure users can move between pages smoothly, like jumping from a leads page to a customer profile in a CRM
*   **Keep the design consistent:** Use the same colors, fonts, and layout so the app feels professional and easy to use

Once you have that solid foundation, add new features one at a time.

*   Start small, like adding a form to capture leads or customer data
*   Next, add functionality to store and display those records, like a simple customer list or profile view
*   Continue adding search, filters, or analytics so users can find data quickly
*   Test after each new piece to catch problems early and avoid breaking what already works

This step-by-step approach makes it easier to test changes, fix issues as they arise, and maintain your app’s stability as it grows. Think of it like building with blocks: get the base right, then stack on new pieces carefully so everything stays strong.

## 

[​

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#turn-on-connectors-only-when-you-need-them)

Turn on connectors only when you need them

[Connectors](https://support.bolt.new/integrations/mcp) are a powerful way to give Bolt real-world information from your external tools and data sources. However, adding information to Bolt’s context increases token consumption. We recommend turning on connectors for a project only when you need them. To learn more, see [Best practices for using connectors](https://support.bolt.new/integrations/mcp#best-practices-for-using-connectors).

##

](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency#avoid-repeated-automated-error-fix-attempts)

Avoid repeated automated error fix attempts

## Frequently asked questions

Everything you need to know about the product and billing.

### What are tokens?

Tokens are how Bolt measures the work it does on your project. Bolt uses tokens when it reads your prompts and project files, makes a plan, or writes code. Your plan includes a monthly token allowance, and you can check your balance on the [Subscription & Tokens](https://bolt.new/settings?page=subscription-and-tokens) page anytime.

For tips to help your tokens go further, see [Maximizing token efficiency](https://support.bolt.new/prompting/maximizing-token-efficiency).

### How do Teams plans work?

Teams plans give you centralized billing, team settings, and a shared workspace for collaborating on Bolt projects. You pay per team member, and paid members get a monthly token allowance based on your plan. Tokens aren’t shared between members. You can also add free members who can view team projects. But since free members don’t get tokens, they can’t send prompts.

### Do tokens roll over from month to month?

On paid plans, yes. Unused tokens from your monthly allowance stay in your balance for up to two months, as long as your paid subscription is active. Free plan tokens don’t roll over. To see how token rollover works with examples, check the [Token rollover FAQs](https://support.bolt.new/account/tokens#token-rollover).

### What’s the difference between monthly and annual billing?

With an annual plan, you pay for the full year up front at a discounted price. With a monthly plan, you pay month by month. In both cases, your token allowance refreshes once a month, and any tokens you don’t use stay in your balance for up to two months after you receive them.

### Can I change my plan later?

Yes. Go to the [Subscription & Tokens](https://bolt.new/settings?page=subscription-and-tokens) page, click **Billing details**, click **See all available plans**, and then pick the plan you want. Upgrades apply right away, and downgrades start at your next billing date. On an annual plan, that date is your annual renewal.

### Can I cancel my subscription?

Yes, anytime. Go to the [Subscription & Tokens](https://bolt.new/settings?page=subscription-and-tokens) page, click **Billing details**, then click **Cancel subscription**. Your plan and unused tokens stay active until your current billing period ends, then your account moves to the Free plan.

If you change your mind, you can [undo a cancellation](https://support.bolt.new/account/billing#undo-a-cancellation) before it goes into effect.

### What are the token limits on the Free plan?

The Free plan includes 1 million tokens a month, with a daily limit of 300,000. Free plan tokens don’t roll over.
